Where: route /crash
Problem: An uncaught exception was thrown 4 times while exercising /crash: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'apiKey'). Whatever was rendering when it threw did not finish, so the user sees a blank or partial view. Route records where the event was observed; its originating route is unverified and may be an earlier view.
Evidence: message=Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'apiKey'), source=at http://localhost:5173/src/pages/Crash.jsx:24:26, routes=/crash, attribution=observed_route, occurrences=4
Fix: Fix the throwing code path and guard the data it assumed. Most mount-time exceptions are an assumption about data that is not true yet: reading a property off a value that is still undefined on first render, or destructuring an API response before it arrives. Guard the access, give the state a sensible initial value, and handle the loading case explicitly. Reported at: at http://localhost:5173/src/pages/Crash.jsx:24:26.
Action: reproduce this by loading /crash, fix the cause described above, then re-run `vibeguru run` to confirm the finding is gone.

findings.ai_prompt:
[Vibe Guru finding: render_loop]
Where: route /render-loop
Problem: /render-loop mutates the DOM ~6212 times/second for as long as it is mounted, in 3 of 3 visits. A view that has finished rendering goes quiet; one that keeps mutating is re-rendering in a loop and will pin a CPU core.
Evidence: mutations_per_second=6212, visits_affected=3/3
Fix: Break the state-update cycle in the component's effect. Look for a useEffect that sets state it also depends on, a missing or incorrect dependency array, or an object/array literal recreated every render and passed as a dependency (use useMemo/useCallback, or move the value outside the component).
Action: reproduce this by loading /render-loop, fix the cause described above, then re-run `vibeguru run` to confirm the finding is gone.

fix.hint: Look for a useEffect that sets state it also depends on, a missing or incorrect dependency array, or an object/array literal recreated every render and passed as a dependency (use useMemo/useCallback, or move the value outside the component).
fix.summary: Break the state-update cycle in the component's effect

findings.ai_prompt:
[Vibe Guru finding: detached_dom_leak]
Where: route /detached
Problem: Visiting /detached retains ~9000 DOM nodes per visit that survive GC (node recovery 0%). Unbounded — node count climbs every cycle.
Evidence: node_recovery_ratio=0.0, nodes_per_visit=9000, nodes_total_retained=27000
Fix: Free per-mount allocations and remove references on unmount. Look for nodes/objects created on mount and pushed into a module-global, ref, or closure that outlives the component. Add cleanup in the useEffect return (or componentWillUnmount).
Action: open the component rendered at /detached, find the cause described above, apply the fix, and ensure the effect cleanup releases everything acquired on mount.

fix.hint: Look for nodes/objects created on mount and pushed into a module-global, ref, or closure that outlives the component. Add cleanup in the useEffect return (or componentWillUnmount).
fix.summary: Free per-mount allocations and remove references on unmount

findings.ai_prompt:
[Vibe Guru finding: listener_leak]
Where: route /charts
Problem: Visiting /charts retains ~5 event listener(s) per visit that are never removed. jsEventListeners grows monotonically across cycles.
Evidence: listener_recovery_ratio=0.0, listeners_per_visit=5, listeners_total_retained=15
Fix: Remove listeners/subscriptions on unmount. Every addEventListener / subscription created on mount must be removed in the useEffect cleanup (return () => removeEventListener(...)). This app uses a chart library — if this view renders a chart, also call chart.destroy() in the cleanup; Chart.js attaches its own window resize listener.
Action: open the component rendered at /charts, find the cause described above, apply the fix, and ensure the effect cleanup releases everything acquired on mount.

findings.ai_prompt:
[Vibe Guru finding: failed_request]
Where: route /bad-fetch
Problem: A network request failed 4 times on /bad-fetch: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED — http://127.0.0.1:49999/api/user-settings. Any view depending on that response renders empty, stale, or stuck in a loading state.
Evidence: message=net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED — http://127.0.0.1:49999/api/user-settings, source=http://127.0.0.1:49999/api/user-settings, routes=/bad-fetch, attribution=request_origin, occurrences=4
Fix: Make the request succeed, and handle the failure case in the UI. Check the URL, method and payload against the actual endpoint — a wrong path or a missing base URL is the usual cause. Then make sure the calling component renders an error state instead of hanging, so a future failure is visible rather than silent.
Action: reproduce this by loading /bad-fetch, fix the cause described above, then re-run `vibeguru run` to confirm the finding is gone.

findings.ai_prompt:
[Vibe Guru finding: retained_instances]
Where: route /observers
Problem: every visit to /observers leaves ~1 live ResizeObserver instance(s) alive after garbage collection (3 across 3 visits). Each observer keeps firing and retains everything its callback closes over.
Evidence: class=ResizeObserver, instances_per_visit=1, instances_total=3
Fix: call observer.disconnect() in the effect cleanup, and make sure nothing outside the component still holds the reference.
Action: open the component rendered at /observers, release the ResizeObserver in its unmount/cleanup path, then re-run to confirm the count stops growing.

fix.hint: call observer.disconnect() in the effect cleanup. The count rising on every visit means the reference outlives the component — check for one held in a ref, a module-level variable, or a closure passed to something longer-lived.
fix.summary: Release the ResizeObserver when the view unmounts

findings.summary: Visiting /observers leaves ~1 live ResizeObserver instance(s) behind every time (3 total across 3 visits). They survive garbage collection, so nothing will reclaim them — each observer keeps firing and retains everything its callback closes over.
findings.title: ResizeObserver instances retained on /observers
